candidate.answerReason: The aisle length is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose opposite leg at 30° is the 2.5 m perpendicular width. Hence the aisle length is 2.5/(1/2) = 5 m.

methods.label: Use the sine ratio
methods.explanation: The length \(x\) occupied along the driving aisle satisfies \(2.5=x\cdot\sin30^\circ\), so \(x=2.5\div\frac{1}{2}=5\) m.
methods.levelReason: Using a sine ratio to recover a hypotenuse is within Grade 9.

methods.label: Use the 30° right-triangle property
methods.explanation:
Let \(L\) be the aisle length between the two marking lines. Draw a perpendicular from one aisle intersection to the other marking line. The resulting right triangle has hypotenuse \(L\), a \(30^\circ\) angle, and opposite leg \(2.5\) m. Since the leg opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse,
\[
L=2(2.5)=5\text{ m}.
\]
Thus each space occupies \(5\) m along the aisle.
methods.levelReason: This route uses the Grade 8 half-hypotenuse property instead of a trigonometric ratio.
